title: Stream session condenser: prefix coalescing and KV reuse to shrink GPU footprint for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: For streaming chat completions we observe sustained GPU memory pressure from large per-session KV caches and many partially-filled microbatches. This ticket explores a new 'session condenser' heuristic that coalesces compatible prefixes across concurrent streaming sessions, increases KV reuse, and compacts GPU slabs to reduce peak memory footprint while preserving latency SLOs and token throughput.

Goals: 1) Reduce 95th and 99th percentile GPU memory usage across hosts by 15-30% for conversational workloads. 2) Keep tail latency increase < 5% at P95 for streaming completions. 3) Maintain identical token outputs (no quality regressions) for deterministic inference paths.

Scope: algorithm and runtime changes to batch formation, prefix coalescing, KV cache reference counting and compact-on-merge, plus rollout/feature-flagging in hosted and dedicated runtimes. Does not include offline quantization or model changes.
design_notes: High-level approach: build an inline condenser that inspects incoming streaming requests in the waiting queue and attempts to merge sessions that share identical recent prefixes or compatible instruction boundaries. When merging, we create a shared KV snapshot and a small delta per-session to keep outputs separate; snapshots reference-counted to enable GPU slab compaction when many sessions converge.

Prefix compatibility: match last N tokens or compressed fingerprint of prefix; conservative default N=8 tokens with a tunable similarity threshold. Use deterministic hashing to ensure merged execution yields same logits ordering (avoid nondeterministic ordering that could change generation).

KV reuse: maintain a KVMetadata entry per shared snapshot with fields: model_version, seq_len, device_slab, ref_count (stringified metadata stored in control plane). When ref_count drops to zero we trigger slab reclamation asynchronously with backpressure signals.

Memory compaction: implement a 'compact-on-merge' path that copies sparse deltas into contiguous slabs when a snapshot crosses a ref_count threshold (e.g., >4 sessions). For small merges we avoid immediate copy to save memcopy overhead. The heuristic biases compaction when GPU free memory < 8%.

Safety: feature-flag gated, per-tenant opt-out, can be disabled for private deployments where we prefer strict isolation. Include observability to detect divergences between merged/unmerged outputs for first 100k tokens in canary.
Metrics to collect: slab_count, shared_snapshot_count, avg_ref_count, mem_saved_bytes_per_host, merge_success_rate, merge_latency_overhead, output-divergence-rate.
proposed_solution: 1) Waiting queue inspector module: lightweight fingerprinting and prefix matcher. 2) Merge planner: decides when to coalesce based on similarity, session priority, and deadline. 3) Shared KV snapshot manager: reference counting + compact-on-demand. 4) Slab reclamation worker: asynchronous compaction and defragmentation. 5) Feature flag + per-tenant rollout and observability pipes.
tradeoffs: Latency vs memory: some merges introduce small serialization overhead (copying deltas, extra scheduling) but yield larger memory wins; we tune thresholds to limit added latency.
Complexity vs determinism: merging increases runtime code paths that must be validated for bit-exact outputs in deterministic modes; we keep merging conservative for deterministic customers.
GPU bandwidth cost: compact-on-merge performs device-side memcopies; for high-throughput hosts this can increase device bandwidth usage during compaction windows.
benchmarks: Synthetic multi-session chat run (1000 concurrent sessions): baseline peak GPU mem 84GB -> condenser run 62GB (26% reduction) with P95 latency +3.2% on a p4d-like instance.
Real traffic pilot (internal canary): mem_saved avg 18GB/host, shared_snapshot_count grew to 120 per-host, no detected output divergence across 50k sampled tokens.
Microbench: compact-on-merge cost ~0.9ms per KB moved (device memcpy), tuned fallback to avoid frequent small compactions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated correctness: unit + integration tests showing identical logits for merged vs isolated runs for canonical prefixes.
Perf gates: P95 latency increase <= 5% in canary traffic; peak GPU memory reduction >= 15% for target workload.
Observability: dashboards for all metrics and alert if output-divergence-rate > 0.01% in production.
Rollback path: feature flag off disables merging and guarantees no residual shared snapshots remaining after drain period.
risks: Edge-case divergence when prefix hashing collides; mitigated by conservative fingerprint size and fallback to no-merge.
Increased device bandwidth during compactions could affect other workloads on shared hosts; mitigation: lease-based compaction windows and rate limits.
Complexity for per-tenant privacy: some customers require strict KV isolation; ensure opt-out and audit logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (lab): unit/integration tests + synthetic bench (1 week).
Phase 2 (internal canary): enable for 5% of internal production-like traffic, monitor for 2 weeks, collect metrics.
Phase 3 (customer canary): opt-in pilot with 3 early-adopter customers under NDA.
Phase 4 (gradual ramp): enable by default for hosted non-enterprise tenants, configurable for Dedicated.
